claims.text: Applying SCCP to a tungsten-based refractory multi-principal-element alloy can simultaneously enhance room-temperature strength and tensile ductility.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that cause premature crack initiation.
SCCP can overcome the conventional strength-ductility trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
A W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloy is an example of the targeted brittle tungsten-based refractory multi-principal-element alloy.
The initial cast or additively manufactured alloy has a bcc structure and coarse grains.
The initial alloy is susceptible to premature cracking from stress concentrations at incoherent interfaces or grain boundaries.

A multi-stage thermomechanical route using controlled aging or precipitation treatments can nucleate and grow coherent nanoprecipitates with a selected lattice mismatch and orientation relationship to a bcc matrix.
The proposed route is distinct from standard solution annealing or simple aging.
The SCCP alloy should retain high strength at 800 degrees Celsius.
Controlled cooling rates ensure stepwise-controllable precipitate formation.
SCCPs possess coherent interfaces with the matrix and serve as sites for dislocation transmission rather than acting solely as barriers.
Dislocation transmission across coherent precipitate-matrix boundaries relieves local stress concentrations and suppresses premature crack initiation.
The coherent precipitates enable strain hardening while preserving plastic deformation.
The processed alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength above 1.0 GPa.
The processed alloy will have room-temperature tensile ductility above 10%, with approximately 15% demonstrated in the cited system.
The processed alloy will maintain a high yield strength at 800 degrees Celsius.
Single-principal-element tungsten alloys have difficulty overcoming the strength-ductility trade-off because of brittle bcc W-enriched phases.
Standard solution annealing or simple aging typically produces either coarse incoherent crack-nucleating precipitates or insufficient strengthening.
Excessive lattice mismatch or an unstable precipitate phase would prevent the proposed coherent-precipitation mechanism.
Incoherent precipitates that induce Orowan bowing rather than dislocation transmission will promote interfacial crack initiation.
